item.research_question: What are the effects of hydrogen on the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) and how can their resistance to hydrogen embrittlement be improved?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), including CoCrFeMnNi, CoCrFeNi, FeCuCrMnMo, and CoCrNi medium-entropy alloys
item.processing_route: Various methods, including vacuum arc melting (VAM), additive manufacturing (AM) techniques such as selective laser melting (SLM), electron beam melting (EBM), and Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF)
item.test_conditions: Hydrogen charging, tensile testing, and microstructural analysis
key_findings: HEAs exhibit unique multi-principal-element compositions, which give rise to four key effects: the high-entropy effect, severe lattice distortion effect, sluggish diffusion effect, and cocktail effect

The lattice distortion effect in HEAs hinders the stable diffusion of hydrogen atoms into the matrix, resulting in a significantly higher hydrogen concentration on the alloy surface than in the interior
The presence of hydrogen in HEAs can lead to a reduction in ductility and an increase in brittleness, but some HEAs exhibit excellent resistance to hydrogen embrittlement
The addition of certain elements, such as Cr and Mo, can enhance the resistance of HEAs to hydrogen embrittlement
The microstructure of HEAs, including the presence of twins and grain boundaries, can play a significant role in determining their resistance to hydrogen embrittlement
item.mechanism: The mechanism of hydrogen embrittlement in HEAs is complex and involves the interaction of multiple factors, including hydrogen diffusion, lattice distortion, and microstructural features
item.limitations: Current research has not fully elucidated the interactions between multi-scale defects and hydrogen transport/accumulation in HEAs
item.future_work: Further research is needed to develop a deeper understanding of the mechanisms of hydrogen embrittlement in HEAs and to design strategies for improving their resistance to hydrogen embrittlement
quotes: HEAs exhibit unique multi-principal-element compositions, which give rise to four key effects: the high-entropy effect, severe lattice distortion effect, sluggish diffusion effect, and cocktail effect

item.research_question: What strategies can mitigate hydrogen-induced failure in high-entropy alloys?
key_findings: Hydrogen-induced phase transformation mechanisms affect hydrogen activation energy trapping
Oxide films can reduce hydrogen absorption and minimize embrittlement risks
Nano-precipitates can serve as hydrogen traps and enhance HE resistance
item.mechanism: Hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC) and hydrogen-assisted cracking (HAC) are influenced by the synergistic effect of applied stress and hydrogen
item.limitations: The understanding of the mechanisms of hydrogen-induced failure remains limited
item.future_work: Future investigations should prioritize synergistic mechanisms of HE and corrosion, atomistic-scale studies, and multi-mechanism coupled modeling
quotes: Hydrogen-assisted cracking (HAC) in alloys in hydrogen environments differs from hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC) by its emphasis on the synergistic effect of applied stress and hydrogen
The thickness of the oxide film directly influences its physical barrier effect
Nano-precipitates in HEAs have been proven to serve as hydrogen traps, offering the potential to further enhance HE resistance
